claim: Node-wise beam search, which maintains top-B candidates per node, enables more effective exploration of the solution space and yields higher-quality solutions compared to classical TSP, SPT, and naive beam search in graph-based planning for active perception.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by implementing NBS and comparing its performance against TSP, SPT, and DBS on graph-based planning benchmarks for active perception tasks.

conditions: tasks including point collection, surface reconstruction, and volumetric exploration
exclusions: limited to the reported graph environments and active perception tasks; transfer beyond them is unestablished

title: Node-wise beam search algorithm for solution quality and more

claim: Microwave power during PECVD growth of vertical graphene nanosheets has a non-monotonic effect on growth rate and crystalline size: initial increase up to an optimum power (375 W) due to increased C2 radical availability and optimum C/H ratio, followed by a decrease at higher powers due to increased hydrogen species that reduce C2 density and etch carbon species.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by growing VGNs at different microwave powers while keeping other parameters constant and measuring growth rate and crystalline size via SEM and Raman spectroscopy.

conditions: Other parameters held constant as in study
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported MW-PECVD system, substrate materials, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Variation of microwave power for Growth rate and crystalline

claim: Under the same assumptions, the L∞ norm of the difference between the classical and relativistic solutions is bounded by C/c^2, with constant independent of c.
falsifier: One can numerically compute solutions of both systems for large c and verify that the L∞ difference scales as 1/c^2.

conditions: local existence of both solutions on [0,T]
initial data sufficiently close to constant states
exclusions: limited to the regime where both relativistic and classical Euler equations have local classical solutions and the initial data are small perturbations of constant states

title: Increasing the speed–convergence of relativistic solution principle
